abstract: Surveillance of functional centers in the mature 60S ribosomal subunit by SBDS licenses its translational debut. Timely release of eIF6 from 60S by SBDS is essential to permit 40S joining. Biallelic mutations in SBDS associated with Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS), an inherited ribosomopathy, impair dissociation of eIF6 from 60S. How SBDS variants that bind to 60S structurally perturb the maturation and surveillance of 60S is yet to be deciphered. Here, we report high-resolution cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of human SBDS and pathogenic variants in complex with human 60S. The structures reveal that disease mutations disrupt key interactions of SBDS with the functional centers of the 60S subunit destabilizing critical bases and protein interactions across the P-site, peptidyl transferase center, polypeptide exit tunnel and GTPase-associated center. These mutations remodel the N-terminal contacts with 60S, altering critical interactions with uL16 (RPL10) distant from the mutation site. Mutations in domains II and III trigger conformational changes that propagate across the entirety of SBDS and remodel distant ribosomal regions, revealing an elegant mechanism of pathogenic allostery. The profound effects of SBDS mutations on both the surveillance and mature conformation of the 60S subunit provide a structural framework for understanding the molecular pathology of SDS.
